multiplayer.note: Transport-agnostic authoritative server with explicit development/raw-UDP and production/QUIC-TLS profiles, 60 Hz authority, 20 Hz acknowledged deltas/keyframes, prediction, ownership, and combat. Protocol 8 rejects mismatched content; optional HMAC supplies client authentication on either profile. One authoritative registry owns session tokens and timeout cleanup; secure-random failures fail closed and keyed disconnects require credentials. GameState includes restart round and authoritative mover tick positions; sequenced commands from old rounds are discarded. Bounded partial-world replication retains one acknowledged baseline and one retryable packet per peer, respects active payload limits, rotates fair/priority records and peers, and exposes queue/delivery counters. Supports 1024 relevant records with individually budgeted records; replication and resync are bound to sessions (since protocol 7). See HOSTING.md for limits and RTT tradeoffs. Server capacity is configurable (with_max_players, --max-players); replication sizes candidates by arithmetic and prepares peers on several threads (with_network_threads, --network-threads) with identical bytes at any thread count (ADR 0027). Replication prioritises nearby records and measures freshness (mean_wait); the server takes time from a Clock so timeouts/reconnect are testable without sleeping; viewer::spans + be2-headless --profile report where a tick goes (ADR 0028). World updates (Snapshot/Delta) are a compact exact binary form, protocol 8, about 5x smaller per player record (ADR 0029). be2-headless stops cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP (final autosave, exit 0; a second signal forces exit 130) without the ctrlc crate (ADR 0030).

contract.performance: One baseline and one retryable packet per peer; active transport payload ceiling

constraints.text: Commit only exactly acknowledged represented state; budget each packet against the active transport limit. Queued bytes are not delivery.

prop_physics.note: Runtime catalog-prop extraction; 120 Hz Rapier compound bodies with per-player authoritative ownership. Large furniture/wall art remain fixed. All eligible bodies are allocated up front (no runtime spawn/despawn, no contact events, no joints; a game needing them owns its own rapier world via vesper3d::rapier); lifecycle sleeping is not lazy allocation. Index-based accessors (prop_index bridges from IDs): mass, half extents, centre of mass, throw_for_player (uncapped release), set_floor (movable/removable implicit ground, kept across restores).

weapons.note: Scientist primary wrench and scroll-selected black pistol with infinite ammo prototype, hitscan raycasts, recoil, muzzle flash, third-person aiming and audio.

fps_foundation.note: Rendering-independent FPS domain: validated catalogs, ten-firearm starter armory, deterministic fixed-tick fire/reload/burst timing, reproducible spread, smooth ADS/FOV, operative archetypes, and authoritative team deathmatch health/scoring/respawns. Games own presentation, hit-shape policy and their transport shell.

arena_shooter_foundation.note: Opt-in, rendering-independent arena FPS layer: validated accelerated ground/air movement, configurable grounded step-up, friction, held-jump momentum chaining, 90-degree camera policy, launch volumes, timed pickups, deterministic projectiles and splash falloff, armor, free-for-all frags and fixed-tick respawns. Existing default movement remains unchanged.

prototype_api.note: SceneBuilder requires an explicit spawn (or without_spawn for a props-only world) and batches ordinary map edits; box_body includes a semantic ID while structural_box creates visual collision without a reachability target. World prop accessors use IDs (position/origin, centre of mass, mass, half extents, rotation, velocities, sleep, holder, hit_prop) with prop_index bridging to the index-based PropPhysics API; throw releases a carried prop at an exact velocity; set_prop_floor moves or removes the implicit y = 0 ground under props. vesper3d::rapier re-exports the pinned physics crate. HeadlessWorld supports transactional map/game replacement with player respawn; network hosts must coordinate content changes. No generic scripting or arbitrary dynamic mesh builder.

constraints.text: External games compile against the supported vesper3d prelude; do not invent private APIs.

native_discovery.note: describe and bounded search use the CLI command registry and embedded feature index. export-lab creates a validated authoring starter. Evidence names and files must resolve; their tests run in the ordinary CI suite.

game_documents.note: GameDocument v1: movement profile, spawns, bounded interaction rules/counters and server-owned objective state (won or lost: complete/fail). Rule conditions are counter comparisons, modulo and all/any/not (ADR 0023). Eligibility and presentation visibility are independent replicated states; hidden entities retain collision. Native game-describe/schema/validate/example; --game on client and headless. No scripting or physical doors. add-interactable creates a target's map and game records together (dry run unless --write). game-explore searches reachable rule states (winnable, shortest win/loss, dead rules, stuck states) using GameRuntime itself (ADR 0024). game-validate names the missing or mismatched map record of an interactable or mover; game-explore flags once-exhausted retries. Movers carry a grounded player standing on them (Controller::ride, ADR 0026).

custom_clients.note: Documented application-owned window/render/input boundary over BlueEngine-owned fixed simulation, including the supported Macroquad version for external crates. docs/CUSTOM_CLIENT.md also covers games that own their simulation (custom-sim, devkit, kit).

Cargo.lock is seeded from the engine's (versions match what the engine was tested with; the first Cargo command settles it) and the engine commit is recorded in assets/identity.json. Path dependencies are not revision pins.

Verification reuses the game's own scripts/check.py; a prior report.json is never treated as current evidence. Never edits the game, switches a checkout, builds, or touches the network.

Authored objectives, timers, movers, dynamic props and win/restart run through the same simulation. Replication carries round identity and mover positions (since protocol 7). custom_simulation.note: For games whose rules are Rust, not GameDocument: enemies, projectiles, scoring, AI, waves, per-frame physics. Scaffold with new-game NAME DIR ENGINE_PATH custom-sim. Graphics-free devkit: FrameClock (wall-clock frame length; get_frame_time() is bumpy under vsync), FixedStepper, InputAccumulator (one input per tick, edges once), Simulation + StateHasher + assert_deterministic, Playback/Timeline/CapturePlan/PerfReport for --playback/--script/--capture/--perf, seeded Rng, Juice, atomic Settings/Records files, Snapshot (save states: F5/F9, autosave, migrations, all-or-nothing loads), synth (procedural audio). The game owns its single authoritative loop; do not stretch GameDocument into scripting.

client_kit.note: Opt-in renderer parts for a game that draws its own world, each independent and without genre logic: View (camera, screen projection), Template/Batch/Tint (small meshes packed per frame into few draw calls), Look/Materials (lit + fog + glow world material, alpha and additive effects, sky; presets daylight/dusk/night), Fx (particles, rings, fireballs, beams, popups, banners), hud (scaled outlined text, panels, bars, vignette, crosshair), SoundBank (off-thread rendered effects and music stems, backend woken during loading), capture::save_frame (reports the real pixel size). PlanarMirror owns a depth-backed target, off-axis aperture projection, near-plane clipping and reflection UVs. PointLight adds four bounded unshadowed local lights per pass, cleared by set_scene for compatibility.

game_shipping.note: Every game ships as a package with its own identity, by script: assets/identity.json (title, tagline, controls, packaging), a title-seeded icon set (be2-tools icon TITLE DIR [VARIANT] [--replace]) used as the exe resource icon (build.rs + rc.exe), the window icon, dist/<exe>.ico and the shortcut icon, scripts/ship.py package/shortcut/verify/ship, a desktop shortcut named after the game that targets dist/ (never target/), tooltip = tagline + controls, verified by reading it back, rendering the shell icon, checking distinctness from every other desktop shortcut, and launching through it. scripts/check.py ends with this ship gate; --skip-ship iterates without it, no desktop is reported as skipped, never as a pass.

save_state.note: Native save states for every tier. One framed, versioned file (SHA-256 over every byte, atomic write with a last-good .bak, named slots, autosave ring, payload migrations, content-fingerprint binding); engine worlds (HeadlessWorld::save_bytes/restore_bytes: players, rules, props, lifecycle; not rapier internals) with a checksum-verified, all-or-nothing restore; GameSession F5/F9 and --load/--save-dir in the stock client; DedicatedServer::with_autosave and be2-headless --load/--autosave; devkit::Snapshot for custom simulations with assert_resumes_exactly, and for physics-backed ones (ADR 0018: contact caches are unsaved history, isolated by experiment) assert_loads_replay_identically plus assert_resumes_within; the promise is declared once as Snapshot::POLICY (SavePolicy::Exact or PhysicsContinuation, ADR 0019), recorded in every save, shown by save-info and proved by assert_resumes_as_promised, which the starter's save test calls; Simulation::hash_parts makes a failed restore name the differing part; be2-tools save-info. What happens after a load depends only on the file. Online clients never save.

contract.owns: The save file format, atomic writes, slots and backups, verification, migrations, world capture/restore, and the all-or-nothing load
contract.inputs: A running HeadlessWorld or Snapshot simulation; save-file bytes
contract.outputs: Framed save bytes, typed SaveError naming the differing hash part, a restored simulation identical to the saved one (and to the uninterrupted run where physics is at rest or falling)
contract.performance: One JSON pass each way; a Test Lab world saves in single-digit milliseconds

constraints.text: A save never replaces a good file with a partial one, and a file whose bytes do not verify is never loaded.

netplay.note: Online play for custom-sim games. NetGame supplies rules, layouts and seats; ClientView supplies prediction and interpolation; NetServer/NetClient supply lobby, sessions, input bundles, snapshots, events, bot handoff, per-match telemetry (matches.jsonl) on any DatagramTransport (UDP, QUIC/TLS, in-memory LoopNet). net::codec is the bounds-checked binary Writer/Reader. Extracted from Spooky Kart; toy.rs is the smallest complete game.

contract.owns: Lobby, sessions, input streaming, snapshot pacing, event delivery, bot handoff and match statistics for a game
contract.inputs: A NetGame implementation and a DatagramTransport
contract.outputs: An authoritative match and clients that predict and interpolate
contract.performance: One snapshot per client every SNAPSHOT_EVERY ticks, each within 1,200 bytes

closed_path.note: ClosedPath: a smooth closed loop on the ground plane (race track, patrol route, rail) with length, point/tangent at a distance, progress and lateral offset of any position, arc distance with wrap-around; plus yaw helpers (forward, right, yaw_of, wrap_angle) in the engine's convention (yaw 0 faces -Z).

rendering_traps.note: Template::quad_facing winds a quad to face a normal whatever the corner order; Template::split and Batch::add split a template over the per-mesh vertex limit (9,000) instead of dropping it; a Template past 65,535 vertices panics instead of wrapping its u16 indices. A world that renders as an empty void was one of these.
